name: Fieldwork Studio
what_we_do: A 14-person marketing studio for consumer brands doing £1m-£30m a year: paid social, search, creative that is made to be tested, and the landing pages those ads point at. We work in 90-day blocks, never longer contracts.
facts: Founded in 2017 by Priya Nair (ex-Meta agency partnerships) and Tom Okafor (ex-creative director at a mid-size London agency).
14 people: 5 media buyers, 4 creatives, 2 developers for landing pages, 3 strategists.
About 60% of clients are beauty, food and drink, and home brands; the rest are mixed DTC and a few B2B software companies.
Engagements run in 90-day blocks. A project (a single audit or launch) starts at £8,000; retainers start at £6,500 a month plus ad spend.
Every ad concept we make ships with at least three variants so the account can learn which one works; we retire creative after about three weeks of falling click-through.
First two weeks of every engagement are an audit: ad account, tracking, landing pages and the last 12 months of spend.
We do not do influencer management, PR or TV.
Our honest view: most brands under £5m a year need two things done well (creative testing and the landing page), not nine services.
Clients we can name: Glow Theory (skincare), Tallow & Thyme (candles), Oatside Kitchen (food), Ledgerly (B2B software).

pages.title: Home
pages.what: Headline 'Ads that learn, pages that convert'. Three client logos, a 'what's your biggest headache?' row of chips, a 'roast my site' field.
pages.studio_take: The headache chips are there because the honest answer to 'what do you do' depends on which one you pick: each has its own article and its own case.

pages.title: Services
pages.what: Nine services in a grid: paid social, search, creative production, landing pages, CRO, tracking, analytics, email, strategy.
pages.studio_take: We know nine boxes is too many. Most clients only ever need two of them.

pages.title: Work
pages.what: Case study grid with a 'show me work for: DTC / B2B / Retail' filter: Glow Theory, Tallow & Thyme, Oatside Kitchen, Ledgerly.

pages.title: Glow Theory case study
pages.what: Skincare brand. Paid social and new product pages. Big hero image of a serum bottle in a cold sink.
pages.behind_the_scenes: The serum-in-a-cold-sink shot was a phone photo from the founder's kitchen; it beat the £12k studio shoot by a mile in testing.

pages.title: Tallow & Thyme case study
pages.what: Candle brand. Christmas launch, search and paid social, a gift-finder landing page.
pages.behind_the_scenes: The gift finder was built in four days after the first Christmas ads sent people to a product grid they bounced off.

pages.title: Ledgerly case study
pages.what: B2B accounting software. LinkedIn and search, a demo-booking page.
pages.behind_the_scenes: We cut their LinkedIn targeting from eleven audiences to two; cost per demo halved. The demo page took seven versions; the one that won opened with the question finance leads asked first on sales calls.

pages.title: Pricing
pages.what: Toggle between Project (from £8,000) and Retainer (from £6,500/month plus spend). FAQ on contracts.
pages.studio_take: The retainer-vs-project toggle is a bit of a false choice: most clients start with a project and only then decide.

pages.title: About
pages.what: Founders, team photo, the 90-day block idea.
pages.behind_the_scenes: The team photo is missing whoever was on holiday that week, and the caption admits it.

pages.title: Why your Meta costs went up
pages.what: Article: rising costs usually come from creative fatigue, not the auction; an account running four ads for six months has nothing new to learn from. Links to Glow Theory.
pages.studio_take: It reads a little smug. Glow Theory came to us running the same four ads since spring, so we have seen exactly this, and the fix was more to test, not more budget.

pages.title: Stop sending ads to your homepage
pages.what: Article: one ad, one promise, one page; homepages lose about half of paid traffic in the first five seconds. Links to Oatside Kitchen.
pages.behind_the_scenes: Oatside Kitchen's offer from the ad was three scrolls down their homepage; moving the ads to three offer pages cut cost per first order 38%.

pages.title: The three-week creative rule
pages.what: Article: we retire creative after about three weeks of falling click-through, not three weeks from launch; every concept ships in at least three variants. Links to Glow Theory.
pages.behind_the_scenes: The rule is the one we ran on Glow Theory: 27 creative variants in the first 90 days, anything whose click-through fell for three weeks retired.

pages.title: Oatside Kitchen case study
pages.what: Food brand. Ads moved off the homepage onto three offer pages, one per promise.
pages.behind_the_scenes: The plainest of the three offer pages, a photo of the tub and the price, beat the other two; the founder had wanted to cut it.

pages.title: When your numbers disagree
pages.what: Article: Meta, Google and the shop each count differently; the first two weeks of every engagement are an audit; count the sale, first order or booked demo, not the click. Links to Ledgerly.
pages.behind_the_scenes: Ledgerly is the example: once booked demos were what got counted, search budget moved to the terms that booked them.

results.said: return on ad spend went from 1.6 to 3.1 over two 90-day blocks.
Christmas revenue from paid up 74% on the year before; the gift finder converted at 4.8% against 1.9% for the product grid.
cost per first order down 38% after moving ads off the homepage onto three offer pages.
cost per booked demo halved, from £410 to £205.
